headline: Ancient Persian King's Legacy of Tolerance Finds Home in Atlanta
meta_description: A 29-foot bronze statue of Cyrus the Great, ancient champion of religious freedom, was installed in Atlanta's Pardis Park this week.
summary_short: Atlanta unveiled a 29-foot statue of Cyrus the Great, the ancient Persian king remembered for religious freedom and tolerance—now one of the largest Iranian monuments ou…
body:
This week, crews in Atlanta completed installation of a 29-foot bronze statue of Cyrus the Great, the ancient Persian king whose legacy of religious freedom and human rights resonates across 2,500 years. Standing in Pardis Park alongside monuments to other global champions of justice, the statue weighs approximately 8,000 pounds and sits atop a limestone base shaped like Cyrus's own tomb in Iran. For Rostam Zafari, the nonprofit founder who championed the project for years, there was no better American city for this tribute than the home of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.—both figures defined by visions of peace, coexistence, and dignity for all people.

Cyrus earned his place in history not through conquest alone, but through tolerance. The Cyrus Cylinder, an ancient clay artifact now held in the British Museum, is widely recognized as one of history's first human rights declarations. Cyrus granted religious freedom to those under his rule, and he famously freed the Jewish people held captive in Babylon, allowing them to return home and rebuild their temple—a deed that earned him unique recognition as a messiah figure outside the Jewish faith. That commitment to pluralism inspired the creation of Pardis Park itself, whose name means "paradise" in Persian and already honors freedom fighters from around the world, including Cuban poet José Martí.

Zafari dedicated the project to his grandparents and hopes the statue offers Americans a truer picture of Iran and Iranian culture—one rooted in freedom, music, and joy rather than stereotypes. The sculpture, created by Atlanta artist Stan Mullins over several years, will be formally dedicated this Saturday during Iran Unveiled, a free family festival celebrating Persian culture. For Zafari, the moment represents something that transcends geography: a shared human commitment to the ideals both nations were founded upon.
quick_facts: 29-foot bronze statue of Cyrus the Great installed in Atlanta's Pardis Park
Bronze weighs 8,000 pounds; includes limestone base shaped like his tomb
Cyrus Cylinder recognized as one of history's first human rights declarations
Statue dedicated Saturday at Iran Unveiled, a free family-friendly festival
One of largest Iranian monuments anywhere outside of Iran
